correctness.rationale: Rechecked the complete corrected RESULT.md. In the frozen endpoint proof, exclusion of a two-cycle in the zero set did not exclude a single directed transition between its two points. The repair rules out each arrow independently: x'=x+y rules out either self-arrow, and W is unchanged at a zero of the drift whereas W(P+)-W(P-)=2z>0. Then Q+Q∘F has no zeros, is continuous and coercive, and attains a positive minimum. Direct expansion of the coboundary and completion of the square prove strict-chamber drift; comparison with R+(1+b)R²/2 yields both claimed uniform liminf bounds (not a common transient). Pointwise escape gives no invariant probability by dominated convergence. Subtracting the signed two-cycle residuals gives X=2/(1+b), and their remaining common part gives kz²-az+K=0; both the positive double root and the absence of any earlier positive root are checked. On the cited slice the rational difference is 1/5210. The corrected theorem retains the closed chamber without claiming that escape ceases immediately beyond it.
residual_risks: The endpoint constant is existential; the open gap between escape and first two-cycle onset is not classified.
